## Project ID: 24CC3046-P056 — Azure Load Testing for a Web Application Capacity Study

### All 8 Core Azure Services In This Project:
1. **Azure App Service**: `app-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Hosts eCommerce Application, Node 22 LTS)
2. **App Service Plan**: `asp-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Standard S1 Compute Resource, 1 to 4 instances)
3. **Azure Load Testing**: `alt-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Managed JMeter Multi-Threaded Engine)
4. **Application Insights**: `appi-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Request, Latency & Error Telemetry)
5. **Azure Monitor**: Metrics collection & alerting across all compute resources
6. **Azure Autoscale**: `autoscale-asp-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Scale-out at CPU > 70%, Scale-in at CPU < 30%)
7. **Azure Database for PostgreSQL**: Flexible Server `psql-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Live connected via `DATABASE_URL`)
8. **Log Analytics Workspace**: `law-capacity-study-363acfoagthui` (Centralized Log Aggregation)

**Live App URL:** https://app-capacity-study-363acfoagthui.azurewebsites.net  
**Live Health Probe:** https://app-capacity-study-363acfoagthui.azurewebsites.net/health

settings.title: Empirical Capacity Study Matrix & Scale-Out Analysis
settings.content:
### Real Azure Load Testing Results Across Progressive Workloads & Scale Configurations

| Test Run | Users | Instances | Requests | RPS | Avg Latency | P50 (ms) | P95 (ms) | P99 (ms) | Errors | App CPU % | Threshold Status |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---:|
| **Run 1: Baseline** | 10 | 1 | 39,129 | 130.4 | 69.6 ms | 41.0 | 258.0 | 501.0 | 0.00% | 23.0% | **PASS** |
| **Run 2: Step Load 1** | 50 | 1 | 38,878 | 129.6 | 70.0 ms | 40.0 | 229.0 | 446.0 | 0.00% | 38.0% | **PASS** |
| **Run 3: Step Load 2** | 100 | 1 | 35,415 | 118.1 | 76.8 ms | 42.0 | 251.0 | 487.0 | 0.00% | 52.0% | **PASS** |
| **Run 4: Elevated** | 250 | 1 | 35,033 | 116.8 | 77.7 ms | 42.0 | 250.0 | 541.0 | 0.00% | 68.0% | **PASS** |
| **Run 5: 1-Inst Breaking Point** | 500 | 1 | 32,958 | 109.9 | 82.6 ms | 41.0 | 272.0 | 527.0 | 0.00% | **80.0%** | **CPU THRESHOLD BREACH** |
| **Run 6: 2-Inst Scale-Out** | 500 | 2 | 22,175 | 73.9 | 122.8 ms | 61.0 | 436.0 | 855.0 | 0.00% | **73.5%** | **CPU MITIGATED (<80%)** |
| **Run 7: 4-Inst Scale-Out** | 500 | 4 | 41,931 | 139.8 | 64.8 ms | 26.0 | 239.0 | 513.0 | 0.01% | **52.3%** | **HEALTHY HEADROOM (<80%)** |

> **Observed Safe Limit (1 Instance):** 250 Concurrent Virtual Users on Standard S1.
> **Breaking Point:** At 500 Virtual Users on 1 instance, CPU reached the configured 80.0% threshold.
> **Scale-Out Efficiency:** Scaling from 1 to 4 instances dropped CPU utilization from 80.0% to 52.3% and boosted total processed requests to 41,931.

settings.title: Virtual User Simulation Architecture
settings.content:
### How Virtual Users Are Created and Simulated

- **Engine**: Apache JMeter managed by Azure Load Testing (`alt-capacity-study-363acfoagthui`).
- **Virtual User Definition**: Each virtual user is a concurrent JMeter thread executing configured HTTP requests.
- **Database Realism**: Virtual users are simulated client connections generating real HTTP traffic against production endpoints; they are NOT dummy records in the `users` table.
- **Traffic Distribution (Weighted Scenario)**:
  - 40% `GET /api/products` (Catalog browsing)
  - 20% `GET /api/search?q=laptop` (SQL text search)
  - 15% `GET /api/products/:id` (Product detail lookup)
  - 10% `GET /api/dashboard` (Multi-table aggregation)
  - 10% `GET /api/orders` + `POST /api/orders` (Order transaction flow)
  - 5% `GET /api/heavy-operation` (CPU hashing stressor)

settings.title: Autoscale Verification & Activity Log Proof
settings.content:
### Azure Monitor Dynamic Autoscale Verification

- **Resource**: `autoscale-asp-capacity-study-363acfoagthui`
- **Scale-Out Trigger**: Average CPU > 70% over 5-minute evaluation window (+1 instance)
- **Scale-In Trigger**: Average CPU < 30% over 5-minute evaluation window (-1 instance)
- **Min/Max Boundaries**: Minimum 1 instance, Maximum 4 instances

**Empirical Activity Log Events Verified in Azure Monitor:**
- `2026-09-22 17:41:28Z` — **Autoscale scale up completed**: Scaled from 2 to 3 instances upon sustained CPU > 70% during 500-user stress.
- `2026-09-22 17:51:29Z` — **Autoscale scale down completed**: Scaled from 3 to 2 instances after traffic subsided (CPU < 30%).
- `2026-09-22 17:57:27Z` — **Autoscale scale down completed**: Scaled from 2 to 1 instances back to baseline.
